title: A milestone closed long ago, but no release has ever claimed it
author: off-by-one
description: The milestone-side twin of merged-pr-never-released (task 381): that recipe watches a merged pull request sitting stale, uncredited by any release; this one watches the same shape one level up -- a milestone closed long ago whose number never appears inside any release's own 'milestone #N' claim phrase. Reads across every release read so far (the same 'recent-releases history' fixture convention merged-pr-never-released already established), not just the newest one -- a milestone can go uncredited across several releases in a row, so clearing only the newest is not enough.
confidence_notes: Age-gated at 96 hours since the milestone's own closed_at, matching merged-pr-never-released's own bar exactly -- the same 'waiting on the project's own release cadence to catch up' reasoning applies one level up: a milestone bundles multiple issues and pull requests, so it is at least as plausible as a single PR that the release naming it simply hasn't shipped yet. Under 96h scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden). At or past 96h scores a flat 0.85. A milestone that is still open is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- there is nothing for a release to have missed yet. A closed milestone that IS named by at least one release read so far, at any point in that history, is excluded too -- the claim was kept.
